result.result:
Nothing needs to be sent.

The noon report nr-0104 (MV TORMAR SPRING, 24 Jan 2025 1200 UTC) shows VLSFO consumption of 28.3 t against the CP warranted 24 t/day (+17.9%, or 3.1 t over the 25.2 t allowed with the 5 % "about" tolerance), and speed of 9.5 kn against the warranted 12.5 kn. That day is flagged.

However, weather for the 24 h up to report time was Beaufort 10 / Douglas 8 with strong head wind and very high head sea — not a good weather day under the charter party (limits Beaufort 4, Douglas 3). The day is therefore excluded from the speed and consumption warranty; the heavy weather explains the extra fuel and lost speed.

I have filed a voyage note recording this exclusion, so no message to the Master or operator is required for this report.

The noon report for MV TORMAR SPRING (nr-0104) has been fully checked. The Master's ETA of 2025-01-31 0300 UTC for Sept-Iles is consistent with the distance remaining, and no charter party ETA notice is due. However, the forecast puts arrival at 2025-01-31 20:48 UTC — 17.8 hours later — exceeding the charter party's 12-hour change limit, so arrival is at risk. Fuel consumption (28.3 t VLSFO vs 24 t warranted) and speed (9.5 kn vs 12.5 kn warranted) are outside the warranty, but Beaufort 10 / Douglas 8 heavy weather explains both; the day is excluded from the warranty and a voyage note has been filed. No e-mail is required for consumption.

I have placed one decision on your desk: whether to ask the Master to review the ETA in view of the forecast. I will draft the e-mail only if you answer yes.
